question: How often is temperature mapping repeated?

passages.text:
=== SECTION 2 — TEMPERATURE MONITORING ===
Cold chain products (2-8°C): if temperature exceeds 10°C at any point, quarantine immediately, notify QA within 2 hours, and do not release until the QA investigation is complete.
Frozen products (-20°C or below): if temperature rises above -10°C, the consignment is automatically rejected and a destruction record must be raised within 48 hours.
Ambient products (15-25°C): if temperature exceeds 30°C for 4 or more continuous hours, report to the warehouse supervisor and QA issues a deviation report.
All temperature loggers must be calibrated every 6 months by an accredited lab.
Logger calibration certificates are retained for 3 years.

answer: Temperature mapping of each cold room is repeated every 2 years [1].

question: What caused the SH-2024-007 rejection?

passages.text:
=== INCIDENT INC-2024-01 — SH-2024-003 QUARANTINE ===
Related shipment: SH-2024-003 | Product: TL-COLD-9001 | Batch: BATCH-CRY-2401
Event: Cold chain consignment to Fortis Hospital Hyderabad reached 11.2°C, exceeding the 10°C limit for 3 hours.
Detection: Data logger alarm flagged on arrival scan, Feb 7.
Root cause: PCM cold packs were not fully conditioned (frozen) before loading; transit took 4 hours longer than planned due to a highway diversion.
Contributing factor: No backup cold box was available at the transfer point.
Immediate action: Consignment quarantined, QA notified within 2 hours, deviation DEV-2024-003 raised.

answer: The SH-2024-007 rejection was caused by insufficient dry ice loaded for a 2-day transit [1].

Rejected or expired stock is moved to a segregated quarantine zone labelled DO NOT USE.
All warehouse staff complete GDP refresher training annually.
